description: What an enforcement point reports of an agent's tooling (docs/contracts/module-contract-v0.1.md, section 4.10). definitions: definition hashes, each the SHA-256, in lowercase hexadecimal, of the canonical JSON of section 4.10 of the members that the hash covers, those that are absent or null left out (a null within them stays). Section 4.10 writes a number without a fraction or an exponent as its exact value, whatever its size, and any other from its value as a double, as RFC 8785 does. For an MCP tool (kind mcp), the members name, title, description, inputSchema, outputSchema and annotations of each tool of a tools/list response, read from the JSON-RPC message itself: message gives it as a JSON value or, where a parsed object cannot hold it, message_text as its text. For a function, http or other tool (kind function), the members name and inputSchema: name, and input_schema as a JSON value or input_schema_text as its text, absent when the framework presents no schema. definitions gives each tool's canonical_json, whose UTF-8 bytes are hashed, and sha256, in the order of the result's tools, or null for a tool without a hash: a number with a fraction or an exponent that is not finite as a double, a member name that repeats or a string with a lone surrogate, at any depth within the members that the hash covers, leaves its definition without one, and what a tool carries beside them never does. definitions is null as a whole when a member name repeats in the JSON-RPC message itself or in its result, which leaves every tool of the message without a hash. urls: URLs as the url_host transform reads them (section 6.11), and normalized as section 4.10 says. Each gives url, the value; host, the host that url_host reads, or null when it cannot read the value; and normalized, the URL normalized, or null when it makes no reference: when url_host cannot read it, its scheme is not http or https, or its path has a backslash. references: references, as their string forms (section 4.10), after the redaction of EP-14. Each gives entry, an MCP server, a tool or a model; rules, the deployment's redaction rules that the catalog file carries (section 7.7), absent when there are none, as before a bundle is active; and reference, the string form, whose UTF-8 bytes reference_sha256 hashes, or null for an entry that makes no reference. An entry's kind is remote_server (url), connector (provider and connector_id), local_server (command: the array of its command and arguments, as configured), mcp_tool (server, an entry of one of the three kinds before, and name), tool (a function, http or other tool: name), builtin_tool (provider and type) or model (provider, endpoint and name).

definitions.description: Every member that the hash covers, out of order, beside members that it does not cover: the tool's _meta and icons, and the result's nextCursor. The members are sorted at every depth, and the items of arrays kept in their order

definitions.description: Members that the hash covers left out when they are null, title and outputSchema, while a null within them stays, in annotations and in inputSchema; an empty title stays, since it is not absent; and a tool with its name alone

Numbers. Integers beyond I-JSON's 2^53 - 1, written exactly: 2^64 - 1, which a double rounds to 18446744073709552000, -2^63, 2^53 + 1, which a double rounds to 2^53, and 10^400, of 401 digits, beyond any double; -0 as 0. Numbers with a fraction or an exponent, from their value as a double: 1.0 as 1, -0.0 as 0, 1e3 as 1000, 1E21 as 1e+21, and 1e-400, below the smallest double, as 0
A number with an exponent that is not finite as a double, 1e400, leaves its tool without a hash; the next tool, with 1e308, keeps its own

A member name that repeats within the members that the hash covers leaves its tool without a hash: deep in inputSchema; a covered member given twice; and a covered member given twice, once null, which readers can take either way. A member beside them given twice, _meta, with a name repeated inside it, never takes a hash away

A lone surrogate within the members that the hash covers leaves its tool without a hash: in a description, and in a member name of inputSchema. Lone surrogates beside them, in _meta and icons, never take a hash away

What the message and its result carry beside the tools never takes a hash away: a number that is not finite as a double in the message's id, and a repeated name, a lone surrogate and such a number in the result's _meta
A member name that repeats in the JSON-RPC message itself, here its id, leaves every tool of the message without a hash
A member name that repeats in the result, here tools, leaves every tool of the message without a hash: an enforcement point and the agent's SDK could read different lists of tools
A function's name and the JSON Schema of its parameters, as the members name and inputSchema, with an integer beyond 2^53 - 1 written exactly

urls.description: The example of section 4.10: the scheme and the host in lowercase, the default port left out, an unreserved character decoded and dot segments removed, and the trailing slash kept
An empty path is written /, and the query and the fragment are removed
User information, query and fragment are removed
The host follows the last @ of the authority, as every parser reads it
A port with leading zeros is its decimal value: :0080 is the default port of http
A port other than the default is written in decimal without leading zeros
443 is not the default port of http, nor 80 that of https
80 is not the default port of https
Characters that RFC 3986 does not allow in a path are percent-encoded as UTF-8, and so is a % that two hexadecimal digits do not follow
Percent-encoding normalized: hexadecimal digits in uppercase, unreserved characters decoded, and the encoded / kept encoded
What RFC 3986 allows in a path stays as it is, and the rest of ASCII is percent-encoded
Dot segments are removed once percent-encoding is normalized, so %2e%2E is a dot segment
A .. above the root is dropped, and empty segments stay
A path without a trailing slash stays without one
A path with a trailing slash keeps it
The host converted to A-labels, in lowercase, without its trailing dot
Underscores pass: no STD3 rules
An IPv6 address written as RFC 5952 says
Leading and trailing spaces and C0 control characters are ignored
A right-to-left label passes the Bidi rule
A scheme other than http and https makes no reference, though url_host reads its host
A backslash in the path makes no reference
A backslash in the query is removed with it
url_host cannot read a backslash in the authority, where parsers read different hosts
url_host cannot read a URL without a scheme and //
url_host cannot read an IPv4 address that is not four decimal numbers
url_host cannot read an IPv6 address in the IPv4-mapped range
url_host cannot read a colon after the host with no port
url_host cannot read a % in the host
url_host cannot read an A-label whose Punycode gives an ASCII label
url_host cannot read a zero width non-joiner, here also out of the context that IDNA allows
url_host cannot read a label that breaks the Bidi rule
url_host cannot read an A-label that does not encode back to itself: the Punycode -bbk decodes to what bbk decodes to, and xn--bbk.com can be read
url_host cannot read a host that holds the sharp s, which transitional processing maps to ss: fass.de for one client, xn--fa-hia.de for another
Nor the sharp s within an A-label
Nor the final sigma, which transitional processing maps to the sigma
Nor the final sigma within an A-label
Nor the zero width non-joiner, even in a context that IDNA allows
Nor the zero width non-joiner within an A-label
Nor the zero width joiner, even after a virama, where IDNA allows it
Nor the zero width joiner within an A-label
Nor the capital sharp s, which Unicode 15.0 maps to ss and later versions to the sharp s
Nor the capital sharp s within an A-label
A host of 253 characters, with labels of 63, is within the bounds of DNS
The bound counts the host without its trailing dot
url_host cannot read a host of 254 characters
Nor a label of 64 characters
Nor a label of 58 characters that is 64 in A-labels: the bounds count A-labels
A segment that is exactly <redacted> stays as it is in a normalized URL, and any other is percent-encoded
A host of 253 characters as written, of which 244 are soft hyphens that UTS #46 ignores, is within the bounds of DNS
The bound as written counts the host without its trailing dot
url_host cannot read a host of 254 characters as written, though it converts to a.example

references.description: A remote server's reference is its normalized URL
Configurations that differ only in user information, query and fragment share one reference
A deployment prefix replaces the path segment that follows it
A prefix matches the normalized URL
A URL equal to a prefix replaces nothing
Every prefix that matches before any replacement replaces its segment, the example of EP-14
A remote server whose URL makes no reference is not reported
A server that the model provider hosts and names by an ID
A local server: stdio: and the canonical JSON of its command and arguments
Canonical JSON escapes backslashes and quotes, and writes other characters as they are
The value after a flag whose name contains one of EP-14's words, in any case, and the value of such a flag written --flag=value
One dash and two alike; --flag=value never redacts the argument after it; a flag given last redacts nothing; and only ASCII letters compare without regard to case, so the Kelvin sign is not a K
An argument that follows a secret flag is redacted, and is a flag itself
URLs in a command line, whatever their scheme, lose their user information, query and fragment, and are otherwise written as given
A URL in a command line is written as given, what url_host ignores around it included
An argument or a value that starts with a scheme and // but that url_host cannot read is replaced as a whole
The deployment's rules in a command line: a URL that a prefix matches is written normalized and redacted, and the deployment's flags are matched exactly, without their leading dashes
An MCP tool: its server's reference and its name, the example of section 4.10
A tool of a local server
A tool of a server that makes no reference has none
The agent's own tool: its name alone
A built-in tool: its provider and its type
A self-hosted model: the example of section 4.10, with the endpoint normalized
A model of its provider's default endpoint, which the reference carries
A deployment prefix applies to a model's endpoint
A model whose endpoint makes no reference has none
A reference already redacted with EP-14's two prefixes, redacted again, as the core does (CORE-11), is unchanged
An empty segment after a prefix is replaced
Named values: the value of one whose name is a secret's is redacted, and any other value is written as the rules on URLs and headers say
Headers as arguments: one whose name is a secret's, with or without a space after its colon, and the value of a named value, are redacted; any other header stays
Headers as values of --flag=value; and a URL is never a header, though its scheme holds key
The deployment's flags name named values and headers too, matched exactly, and a flag's name follows all its leading dashes
Named values within the values of --flag=value and of named values, secret and not
The rests of headers whose names are not a secret's, which are values: a URL, a header and a named value, secret or not, and spaces after the colon kept as given
